planet-day.jpg.tool: Gemini app (gemini.google.com), image generation, in David's account
prompts: Create an image: a seamless equirectangular texture map (2:1 aspect ratio, as wide as possible) of the daytime surface of a fictional ocean planet, for wrapping onto a sphere in a 3D game. Deep blue oceans covering about 70 percent, green and ochre continents with mountain ranges, forests and deserts, small island chains, white polar ice caps along the top and bottom edges, no clouds, no text, no grid lines, no border, flat even lighting with no shadows or day-night line, and the left and right edges must join seamlessly.

That day map looks too much like Earth. Please make a new one with entirely invented continents that do not resemble any real Earth landmass: three large irregular continents and several archipelagos, deep blue oceans covering about 70 percent, green and ochre land with mountain ranges, forests and deserts, white polar ice caps along the top and bottom edges. Same format: seamless equirectangular texture map, 2:1 aspect ratio, as wide as possible, no clouds, no text, no grid lines, no border, flat even lighting, left and right edges joining seamlessly.
Good continents, but the map has place-name labels on it. Make exactly the same map with no labels, no words and no lettering anywhere: just the terrain, oceans and ice caps.
planet-day.jpg.note: The first result was plainly Earth and the second had place-name labels; the third is used.
planet-day.jpg.processed: research/station-assets/textures.py: the wrap's edges cross-faded so it leaves no seam; JPEG quality 82

planet-night.jpg.tool: Gemini app (gemini.google.com), image generation, in David's account
prompts: Now the matching night-side map of this same invented planet: exactly the same continents, coastlines and layout, same size and aspect ratio, but at night. Oceans and land nearly black, warm yellow-orange city lights clustered along coastlines and rivers, sparse in deserts and mountains, none on the ice caps. No clouds, no labels, no text, no grid lines, no border, left and right edges joining seamlessly.
planet-night.jpg.note: Checked against the day map: 99% of its city lights fall on the day map's land.
planet-night.jpg.processed: research/station-assets/textures.py: the wrap's edges cross-faded so it leaves no seam; JPEG quality 82

starfield.jpg.tool: Gemini app (gemini.google.com), image generation, in David's account
prompts: Now a separate image: a seamless equirectangular starfield skybox texture (2:1 aspect ratio, as wide as possible) for a 3D space game. Mostly deep navy-black space, thousands of small sharp white and pale blue stars of varied brightness, a faint soft violet and navy nebula band crossing the middle, no planets, no galaxies in close-up, no text, no border, and the left and right edges must join seamlessly.
starfield.jpg.note: Only its nebula is used: research/station-assets/textures.py filters its stars out.
starfield.jpg.processed: research/station-assets/textures.py: the wrap's edges cross-faded so it leaves no seam; JPEG quality 82
